'''Sir John Ashworth''' (27 November 1938 – 3 March 2025) was a British biochemist and [[educationalist]].

==Early life and education==
Ashworth was born on 27 November 1938.<ref name="whoswho">{{cite web |url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U5875 |title=Ashworth, Sir John (Michael) |date= Dec 2010|work=Who's Who 2011 |publisher=A & C Black; online edn Oxford University Press|accessdate=10 March 2011}}</ref> He was educated at [[West Buckland School]] and [[Exeter College, Oxford]].<ref name="whoswho" /> Ashworth obtained a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in biochemistry at [[Leicester University]] and was a lecturer and reader there before taking up a post of foundation Professor of [[Biology]] at [[University of Essex]] in 1974.<ref name="BeaverInterview" /> His scientific research at the time focused on [[developmental biology]] and [[cell differentiation]], with a particular interest in the [[slime mold]].

==Career== 
Ashworth joined the [[UK government]]'s [[Cabinet Office]] in 1976, where he acted as the [[Government Chief Scientific Adviser (United Kingdom)|chief scientific adviser]] to the government, initially on secondment, and then as an [[undersecretary]] in the Cabinet Office from 1979 to 1981. He became vice-chancellor at the [[University of Salford]] from 1981 to 1990,<ref>{{cite journal |title=Think tank steals metal man as chief scientist man|journal=[[New Scientist]]|date=22 October 1981 |volume=92 |number=1276|page=221|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=L4NTyHivbV8C&pg=PA221}}</ref> and then director of the [[London School of Economics]] from 1990 to 1996.<ref name="BeaverInterview">{{cite news |last1=Gutbrod |first1=Hans |title=Interview with John Ashworth, Director of the London School of Economics |url=https://digital.library.lse.ac.uk/Documents/Detail/beaver.-1993-05-04.-vol-379/535349?item=535361 |publisher=The Beaver, LSE Student Newspaper |date=4 May 1993}}</ref> 

Ashworth was a chairman of the [[British Library]] board 1996–2001, the [[Institute of Cancer Research]] (deputy chairman) 2003–07, and [[Barts and the London NHS Trust]] 2003–07.<ref name=Moon-2-January-2008>{{cite news|first=Vanessa |last=Moon|date=2 January 2008  |url=http://www.gazette-news.co.uk/news/1936500.0/ |title=A knight's tale|newspaper=[[Daily Gazette]]}}</ref>

Ashworth was a governor of the [[Ditchley Foundation]] and also chairman of the board of trustees at [[Richmond American University London|Richmond, The American International University in London]], a private liberal arts and professional studies university based in [[Richmond upon Thames]] and [[Kensington]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.richmond.ac.uk/content/admissions/about-the-university/board-of-trustees.aspx|title=Richmond Admissions, Top London University for International Students - Richmond University|website=richmond.ac.uk|access-date=7 February 2011|archive-date=4 January 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090104183120/http://www.richmond.ac.uk/content/admissions/about-the-university/board-of-trustees.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Ashworth married Auriol Stevens on 23 July 1988. He lived in [[Wivenhoe]] in north-east [[Essex]], close to his daughter and grandchildren. He died on 3 March 2025, at the age of 86.<ref>[https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/memorials/death-notices/death/30664486.sir-john-ashworth/notice Sir John Ashworth] Gazette News</ref>

==Honours==
Ashworth was awarded an Honorary Doctor of Laws from the University of Leicester in 2005. He retired in 2007, and was awarded a [[Knight Bachelor|knighthood]] for public services in the [[2008 New Year Honours|Queen's New Year Honours list 2008]].<ref name=Moon-2-January-2008/> He was made an Honorary Fellow of [[Exeter College, Oxford]] in 1983.

John Ashworth was elected membership of the [[Manchester Literary and Philosophical Society]] in 1981 <ref> Society Manchester Memoirs vol 3 1982-84 </ref>
